description.summary: Momo (the Missouri Monster) is a Bigfoot-type cryptid reportedly seen near Louisiana, Missouri in the early 1970s, most famously during a brief 'monster flap' in July 1972.
description.full: Momo, an abbreviation of Missouri Monster, is a regional Bigfoot-type cryptid associated with the area around Louisiana, Missouri, in northeastern Missouri (Pike County) along the Mississippi River. Witnesses described a large, hair-covered, bipedal creature roughly seven feet tall, with a 'pumpkin-shaped' head, glowing orange eyes, and a strong putrid smell. The most widely publicised sightings occurred in July 1972, including a 11 July 1972 incident in which two young brothers playing in their backyard and their older sister, who saw the creature from the kitchen window, reported a hairy creature carrying a dead dog. Local fire chief and city council member Richard Allan Murray was among other witnesses. A roughly 20-person posse searched the area but found no specimen. The active sighting period was brief and Momo became a fixture of regional folklore and 1970s American 'monster flap' culture, including a Six Flags theme-park ride (1973-1994) and a 2019 docudrama film.

history.modern_era: Momo today is primarily a piece of regional Missouri folklore and a touchstone of 1970s 'monster flap' history. Louisiana, Missouri continues to celebrate the Momo legend through occasional festivals and tourism, and cryptozoological writers regularly include Momo in surveys of regional Bigfoot variants.

notable.name: Louisiana, Missouri backyard sighting
notable.description: An older sister identified in Wikipedia as Doris reportedly observed a tall, dark, hair-covered bipedal creature from her kitchen window while her two younger brothers played in the backyard. The creature was reported to be carrying what appeared to be a dead dog and emitted a strong odor.

credibility.notes: The single most widely-cited incident of the Momo flap.

scientific.name: Regional Bigfoot variant
scientific.description: Momo represents a localised expression of the broader Bigfoot tradition, possibly involving the same posited unknown North American hominid.
evidence_cited: Continuity of description with other 1970s Bigfoot-type sightings

skeptical.name: Misidentification and 'monster flap'
skeptical.description: Skeptical commentators treat Momo as a classic localised 'monster flap' driven by a small number of initial sightings, media amplification, and likely misidentification of bears or hoax incidents.
evidence_cited: No further activity in following years

folklore.beliefs: Momo is broadly treated in popular culture as a regional Bigfoot variant; locally it functions both as folk creature and as town mascot.
